concepts.title: Governance and the Need for Rules

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Governance and the Need for Rules' refers to.
questions.a: Where many people live together, disagreements and disorder follow unless there are rules; governance is the process of making and applying such rules so that society keeps order and harmony.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Governance and the Need for Rules'.
questions.a: Rules at home, school and nation scale up into governance: someone must decide, and decisions must apply to all.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Governance and the Need for Rules' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Democracy: Government by the People' refers to.
questions.a: Democracy is a system where the people hold power: they choose their rulers through elections, rulers remain answerable to them, and every adult has a vote and a voice.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Democracy: Government by the People'.
questions.a: In democracy, power flows upward from citizens, not downward from a ruler.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Democracy: Government by the People' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Values of Democracy' refers to.
questions.a: Democracy rests on values: justice, liberty, equality and fraternity, respect for every culture's identity and dignity; without equality there is no justice, and without justice there is no peace, as Rigoberta Menchu Tum says.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Values of Democracy'.
questions.a: Elections alone are not democracy: the values of dignity and equality give elections their meaning.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Values of Democracy' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Dharma Protects: An Ancient Insight' refers to.
questions.a: The Mahabharata verse says the ruler protects dharma and dharma, in turn, protects those who protect it; power exists to uphold right order, and a ruler who upholds dharma is himself safeguarded.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Dharma Protects: An Ancient Insight'.
questions.a: Ancient India already tied ruling to duty: government is legitimate only while it protects the right.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Dharma Protects: An Ancient Insight' taught, and from which source text?
